synopsis: Honda's Collision Mitigation Braking System (CMBS) is its AEB system; the booklet describes investigations of hard braking with nothing in the way as the largest documented production-fleet case of unnecessary automatic braking [f15759, f15758]. NHTSA opened PE22-003 on 21 February 2022 with 278 complaints, including six alleging collisions, and upgraded the case in April 2024 to EA24-002 with 1,294 complaints covering 2,997,604 Accord and CR-V vehicles and their hybrid variants [f1483, f1484, f1485, f1486]. In January 2025, EA25-002 added 295,125 Insight and Passport vehicles; Honda cited about 412 reports, while NHTSA reviewed 475 in total [f1488, f15764]. Honda attributed some complaints to customers misunderstanding the system or its limits, while technicians unable to reproduce faults called the behavior “normal AEB operation”—accounts the booklet places in tension with the complaint record [f1489, f10775, f1970]. The investigation remained unresolved in the booklet, secondary sources reported no recall ordered as of 2026, and crash and injury totals varied substantially between outlets, leaving both outcome and harm counts uncertain [f2015, f1490, f1487, f1961, f2023]. For off-road validation planning, the corpus recommends large sets of apparently dangerous situations that should not trigger braking and treating workshop-unreproducible complaints as early warnings during field pilots [f1992, f15772].
